study_notes.topic: Alphanumeric Series and Alphabet Test (Verbal Reasoning)

sections.title: Level 3 Advanced Strategy
sections.content: In Level 3, multiple conditions are applied simultaneously. Step 1: Clearly write the given word or number group. Step 2: Apply each condition in sequence. Step 3: Write the new form after each step. Step 4: Solve the question based on the final result. Step 5: Do not skip any step, as it may completely change the outcome.

sections.title: Word Sets
sections.content: In word sets, multiple words are given and sequential transformations are applied. Step 1: Write all the given words. Step 2: Apply the first condition (for example, swapping the first and third letters). Step 3: Apply the second condition (for example, replacing vowels with the next letter in the alphabet). Step 4: Analyze the new words formed. Step 5: Count or compare according to the question. Example: CAT → TAC, then since A is a vowel it may change to B.

sections.title: Number Sets
sections.content: In number sets, transformations are applied to multi-digit numbers. Step 1: Write all the numbers. Step 2: Add 1 to the middle digit. Step 3: Subtract 2 from the first digit. Step 4: Form the new numbers. Step 5: Compare them to identify the largest or the second largest number.

sections.title: Complex Multi-Step Shifting
sections.content: In some questions, elements at odd and even positions are changed using different rules. Step 1: Identify elements according to their positions. Step 2: Apply one rule to elements in odd positions. Step 3: Apply another rule to elements in even positions. Step 4: Write the new sequence. Step 5: Determine the answer based on the final arrangement.

sections.title: Interlacing Elements
sections.content: Sometimes odd and even elements are separated and then combined again to form a new order. Step 1: Write elements at odd positions separately. Step 2: Write elements at even positions separately. Step 3: Combine them according to the given rule. Step 4: Form the new series and solve the question.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content: 1. Applying conditions in the wrong order. 2. Not writing the new form after each step. 3. Confusing odd and even positions. 4. Making mistakes in the final comparison.

sections.title: Quick Summary
sections.content: In Level 3, multi-step logic is the most important aspect. Apply each rule in sequence, write the intermediate result after every step, and finally determine the answer based on position or value.

tricks.title: Stepwise Transformation Rule
tricks.explanation: Apply each condition in a separate step.
tricks.example: First swap letters, then change vowels.

tricks.title: Swap Position Shortcut
tricks.explanation: If the first and third letters must be swapped, follow the pattern A B C → C B A.

tricks.title: Vowel Next Letter Rule
tricks.explanation: Replace vowels with the next letter in the alphabet.

tricks.title: Digit Operation Trick
tricks.explanation: Apply the given mathematical operations separately to each digit.

tricks.title: Odd-Even Separation
tricks.explanation: Separate odd and even positions before applying rules.

tricks.title: Write Intermediate Results
tricks.explanation: Write the new word or number after each step.

tricks.title: Comparison Shortcut
tricks.explanation: To quickly compare numbers, first check the hundreds digit.

tricks.title: Position Tracking Method
tricks.explanation: Write the position of each element in long series.
